messages:
jia_customer_eng: Hey team — our Private control plane mTLS started failing after our edge proxy was upgraded last night. Apps get TLS handshake_failure and Redwood shows no client certs. Happens for all instances in our VPC.
elena_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact client error and a short repro? Is this only for control plane endpoints or all outbound mTLS?
jia_customer_eng: Only to controlplane.redwood.internal:443 (private control plane). Error we see in app logs: "tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate". No obvious 403. We tested with curl from app host: `curl -v --cert /etc/redwood/client.crt --key /etc/redwood/client.key https://controlplane.redwood.internal/health` -> connection resets after ClientHello.
elena_support: Can you run openssl s_client with -debug so we can see whether the ClientHello reaches Redwood or if the proxy is terminating? Example we usually ask: `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.crt -key client.key -servername controlplane.redwood.internal -state -debug`
sam_network: Quick question — did the proxy upgrade change from TLS passthrough to TLS inspect/terminate mode? When a proxy intercepts and terminates TLS it will present its own cert to Redwood and not forward the client cert. That will break mTLS.
jia_customer_eng: I asked infra, they said the new version enabled "SSL Deep Inspection" for outbound by default. They're going to check, but in the meantime here's a tcpdump from the app host (redacted IPs):
```
# tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.12.34.56 and port 443 -s 0 -w - | tshark -r - -V | sed -n '1,120p'
05:12:45.123456 IP 10.0.1.12.443 > 10.12.34.56.49152: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 501, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321], length 511
    TLS Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Client Hello
    tls.record.version: 0x0303
    ...
05:12:45.123789 IP 10.12.34.56.49152 > 10.0.1.12.443: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0
```
It looks like we connect to the proxy IP (10.0.1.12) not the backend Redwood instance — so proxy is in-path.

fw_team_sre: Confirmed — our edge proxy is terminating TLS and performing certificate inspection. It uses a local CA to re-sign. That would drop or replace the client cert. For mutual TLS we need PASS-THROUGH.

elena_support: Yep, if the proxy terminates TLS the control plane will never see the client cert. Two options: 1) configure proxy to passthrough connections for the control plane hostnames/IPs, 2) configure proxy to forward the original client certificate via a trusted header (not recommended for mTLS) or 3) allow a network bypass for the control plane IP range.

jia_customer_eng: Do you have a quick test to confirm proxy termination vs passthrough?

sam_network: Run openssl s_client twice: once to controlplane FQDN and once directly to the proxy IP with -servername. Compare the certificate presented. Example:
```
# to FQDN
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.internal:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.internal -showcerts < /dev/null
# to proxy IP
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.1.12:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.internal -showcerts < /dev/null
```
If the certs differ (proxy shows its re-signed cert) proxy is terminating. Also on the app host do `curl -vk --cert client.crt --key client.key https://controlplane.redwood.internal/` and note whether the server requests a certificate or immediately returns a proxy HTML page or closes connection.

jia_customer_eng: Ran those — FQDN shows a subject CN=EdgeProxy-Inspection-CA, proxy IP shows same. Directly hitting the control plane IP (we retrieved from our route table) shows CN=controlplane.redwood.internal and the handshake completes with client cert. So confirmed: proxy is terminating.

elena_support: Thanks for confirming. For Private/VPC setups we recommend bypassing TLS inspection for control plane hosts so client certs reach Redwood. Can you ask infra to add an allowlist rule for destination ports 443 to the control plane prefix (we can provide the CIDR) and set the proxy to passthrough for that prefix?

fw_team_sre: We can add a bypass for the control plane CIDR. One caveat: if the control plane IPs are in a managed DNS pool that can change, use FQDN passthrough rules rather than hardcoding IPs, or use egress ACLs to the Redwood-managed ASN ranges.

jia_customer_eng: Appreciate it. One more question — if we can't bypass the proxy, is there any way to get mTLS working through an intercepting proxy?

elena_support: Practically no. mTLS requires end-to-end client cert exchange at the TCP/TLS layer. If the proxy terminates TLS and re-initiates upstream, it must present the client cert on behalf of the client — which requires the proxy to possess the client's private key (not acceptable). Some proxies support TLS passthrough with SNI-based routing; that will work.

infra-oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-4523 — "Control plane mTLS failures due to outbound TLS inspection" assigned to fw_team_sre.

fw_team_sre: I've pushed a config change to add a passthrough rule for controlplane.redwood.internal via FQDN match and allowed the control plane CIDR. Waiting for rollout (eta ~10m).

jia_customer_eng: After the rollback to passthrough the handshake succeeded, apps healthy again. Thanks all :raised_hands:

elena_support: Great to hear. We'll leave the ticket open for 24h to monitor. If you want, we can share a short doc on recommended egress rules for Redwood Private control plane.

jia_customer_eng: Please do, that'd be helpful.

sam_network: Notes to include: bypass TLS inspection for control plane FQDNs, allow outbound 443 to Redwood control plane CIDR, ensure MTU doesn't cause fragmentation, and avoid proxies that rewrite client certs.

elena_support: Adding that to the follow-up doc. :white_check_mark:
